Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (Brady Hot Springs PoroTomo DAS, March 2016, stride 20):

RECORDS
- Records analysed: 759 (2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 detections above the catalogue Mc)
- Pumping over 15.96 days: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED PROBABILITY — catalogue-based (Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5), using the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue magnitudes (this is the calibrated estimate):
  b     Sigma     P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0   -5.449    0.0001198      5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73  -5.319    0.004922       0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65  -5.281    0.01474        0.0006484                        0.4653

UPPER BOUND — DAS-based, with uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection is counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts (this is NOT calibrated):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue estimate gives a Pohang-like (Mw >= 5.5) probability of at most ~1.5e-2 per year even at the lowest b scenario (b = 0.65), while the DAS-based upper bound is higher (0.078/yr) only because uncalibrated DAS magnitudes over-count events above Mc. The data show no strong evidence of injection-induced seismicity at Brady Hot Springs in March 2016 under the calibrated model.
